claim_lines.91: 2.1 Composition of the two squares. Consider the two commutative squares: $\tau\circ i_*=i_*\circ\tau$ on $X\to\mathbb P^n\times_kY$ by [L1], and $\tau\circ p_!=p_*\circ\tau$ on $\mathbb P^n\times_kY\to Y$ by [L2]. Composing them gives $\tau_Y\circ p_!\circ i_!=p_*\circ i_*\circ\tau_X$, and by the functoriality of both pushforwards, $p_!\circ i_!=f_!$ and $p_*i_*=f_*$, this is exactly $\tau_Y\circ f_!=f_*\circ\tau_X$, the displayed formula. [L1, L2, L3, step 1.1, algebra]

mathematical_check.domains_codomain: For each smooth scheme S among X, P, Y, τ_S maps K₀(S) to A*(S)_Q. The K-theory arrows i_!:K₀(X)→K₀(P) and p_!:K₀(P)→K₀(Y) have compatible sources and targets; the Chow arrows i_*:A*(X)_Q→A*(P)_Q and p_*:A*(P)_Q→A*(Y)_Q do as well. Here i_* denotes Chow pushforward, while the source line's i_* in the GRR expression is the K-theory pushforward i_!.
mathematical_check.composite_paths: Starting from K₀(X), the upper-then-right path followed by τ_Y is τ_Y∘p_!∘i_!. The τ_X-then-lower path is p_*∘i_*∘τ_X. Square commutativity gives equality. Since f=p∘i, functoriality gives p_!∘i_!=f_! and p_*∘i_*=f_*, so the pasted identity is τ_Y∘f_!=f_*∘τ_X.
mathematical_check.notation: The line suppresses subscripts on τ and writes i_* for the K-theory pushforward, whereas the Chow map also uses i_*. This is conventional context-dependent notation, not a demonstrated mathematical defect; the diagram should distinguish i_! from Chow i_*.
mathematical_check.result: Domains, codomains, and both composite paths agree with the stated factorization; no mismatch found.
